title: ScientificClaim/v1
description: A typed scientific statement under epistemic discipline. A claim carries a structured statement (a subject/predicate/object triple or a MathIR reference), a claim_class placing it on the epistemic ladder, a claim_status tracking investigation, an epistemic_source naming how the claim came to be, and support_refs pointing at the supporting objects. CRITICAL INVARIANT: claim_class='established_law_reference' REQUIRES epistemic_source='literature' AND a non-empty support_refs; a claim_class='candidate_hypothesis' can never carry claim_status='supported' without support_refs. These are encoded via allOf/if-then below and re-enforced in srl.semantic.claims at the Python level (defense in depth). The payload also carries the two safety consts (canonical_writes=0, grants_authority=false). Canonical JSON contract: sorted keys, compact separators, UTF-8, no NaN/Infinity, trailing newline.

allOf.$comment: candidate_hypothesis AND status=supported => support_refs non-empty (a hypothesis cannot graduate to supported without support).

claim_id.description: Content-addressed identity: sha256 over the canonical encoding of the claim (without this field), prefixed 'sha256:'. Computed by srl.semantic.claims.claim_id.

statement.description: The structured statement. Either a subject/predicate/object triple or a MathIR reference (an inline expression tree under 'math' or a MathIR object_id under 'math_ref'). The two shapes are mutually exclusive.

subject.description: The subject of the claim (a name or symbol reference).

predicate.description: The predicate relating subject and object (a name or relation symbol).

object.description: The object of the claim (a name, value, or symbol reference).

math.description: An inline MathIR expression tree carrying the mathematical content of the claim. Validated for allowlist compliance by srl.semantic.ir.validate_expression.

math_ref.description: A reference (object_id) to a MathIR/v1 object carrying the claim's mathematical content.

claim_class.description: The epistemic class placing the claim on the ladder: a candidate_hypothesis is a proposal awaiting evidence; a derived_result follows from other claims; an established_law_reference cites a physical law from the literature (REQUIRES epistemic_source=literature and a support_ref); an empirical_observation is a measured fact; a definition is a definitional convention (tautological, not evidence-bearing).

claim_status.description: The investigation status. A proposed/under_investigation claim is open; supported means evidence supports it (a candidate_hypothesis needs support_refs to reach this); refuted means evidence contradicts it; inconclusive means the evidence is mixed.

epistemic_source.description: How the claim came to be: operator (an agent authored it), literature (it cites prior work; REQUIRED for established_law_reference), derivation (it follows by symbolic/numeric derivation), experiment (it follows from a measurement).

support_refs.description: The object_ids of supporting objects (other claims, MathIR, evidence assessments). Empty for an unsupported proposal. Non-empty is REQUIRED for established_law_reference and for a candidate_hypothesis that has graduated to supported.

created_utc.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp at seconds precision (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). No offset, no fractional seconds.

canonical_writes.description: Safety const: a claim is immutable once authored. Always 0; a non-zero value is a contract violation.

grants_authority.description: Safety const: a claim never grants authority on its own. Always false; a true value is a contract violation. A supported claim is still an admission, not an authorization.
